posts.author: MatidiaRM
posts.body:
SYNOPSIS
Three years ago, a catastrophe caused by beings from another dimension took the lives of many innocent people. Today, another anomaly has reappeared in the city and only two young girls can prevent another incident from happening again.
Join Yuki and Ketsudan in this little adventure to save the world from the threats of the “other plane”.
SCREENSHOTS
DEVELOPMENT
“Magic Fury: Prologue” is a game made in RPG MAKER 2003 with the classic turn-based fighting system.
Originally this project was created to be part of a magical girls themed jam, but due to lack of time it couldn't be delivered on the corresponding date. Even so I decided to finish the project because I ended up liking the idea too much. When an idea comes to me, I end up imagining in the long run what will happen with my characters. That's the case of Magical Fury, which was originally called “Prototype”. But the final result of the project made me consider it as a prologue of something that might continue in the future. I'm still not an expert in enemy balance so I hope the game won't be too unbalanced for new players. Ideally, I would like to know what people think about this idea.
GAME TRAILER
​
UPDATE 28.05.26: I'm not happy with how this game turned out. I think that, unlike the others I've made, Magical Fury hasn't aged very well. For this reason, I've decided not to post a download link and to start reworking this project in the future. Sorry if this causes some trouble in the forums.
If the administrators wish, they can delete this thread.

posts.author: spud.z
posts.body:
Spoiler
Hey Matidia! I played through your game and I found it quite charming. The characters were intriguing and animated. I really enjoyed all the custom graphics and thought they brought a lot of character to the project. I can tell a lot of love went into them. The cinematic scene when they were looking on the city was great, so simple yet so striking. The music fit well and the puzzles were simple but serviceable. I didn't find the enemies to be too difficult to deal with and while they were of the typical RPG Maker grindy variety, I found the custom skills you implemented to be entertaining and the damage type variety in enemies was also enough to keep me intrigued. The washing machine was by far my favorite character, especially when she lands on [Cube]. I was devastated when they killed her.
Good stuff!
